claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 16.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 16, there are some important factors to consider. At this age, you can still qualify for Child Benefit if Alex is in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in school, college, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's left school. He's just signed up with the careers service though to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is helpful - the fact that Alex has registered with the careers service is relevant.

According to the rules, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service.

Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**When did Alex leave education, and when did he register with the careers service?** (I need to understand if this was recent and whether the 20-week period would still apply)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school just a few weeks ago, and he registered with the careers service shortly after that - maybe about 2 or 3 weeks ago now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's very helpful.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Has Alex started any paid work? And if so, is it for 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Is Alex currently receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not getting any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's why:**

Since Alex is 16 and recently left school, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for **20 weeks** after he registered with the careers service. As Alex registered only 2-3 weeks ago, you're well within this 20-week eligibility period.

Additionally, all the necessary conditions are met:
- Alex lives at home with you in the UK
- He's not working 24 hours or more per week
- He's not receiving benefits in his own right

**Important to note:** This eligibility will last for up to 20 weeks from when Alex registered with the careers service. After that period, your eligibility would depend on whether Alex enters approved education, training, or other qualifying circumstances.

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit for Alex, or if you need to update your circumstances, you should contact the Child Benefit Office to ensure your payments continue during this 20-week period.
